paragraphs: Menachot 69b relates that wheat came down for him (from the clouds), a kyuba high over three parasangs.

notes.text: The frozen unit is כיובא, kyuba, whereas the consulted Menachot69b has כיזבא, kizba. Rashi describes the height with the words “(שני) טפחים בזקיפת גודל.” The exact source-unit reading remains open; no modern volume or distance conversion is imposed.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 969) has כיובא, kyuba. The consulted Menachot 69b has כיזבא, kizba. Davidson gives a depth of one handbreadth, while the consulted Rashi gloss has “(שני) טפחים בזקיפת גודל,” with “two” in parentheses. The account follows Rabbi Zeira’s question about whether wheat that fell from the clouds could be used for the two loaves.
